questions.q: State the algebraic condition for a pair of linear equations to have a unique solution.
questions.a: For a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, the condition for a unique solution is a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂. A wrong answer (e.g., "a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂" or "a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂") confuses the unique solution case with parallel or coincident lines.

questions.q: Without graphing, determine whether the system 3x + 2y = 7 and 2x + 3y = 8 has a unique solution.
questions.a: Check: a₁/a₂ = 3/2 and b₁/b₂ = 2/3. Since 3/2 ≠ 2/3, the condition a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ is satisfied, so the system has a unique solution. A wrong answer (e.g., "yes, because both equations have the same coefficients") shows the student does not understand the ratio comparison.

questions.q: A system has a₁/a₂ = 5/3 and b₁/b₂ = 5/3. What can you conclude about the number of solutions?
questions.a: Since a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂, the lines are either parallel (no solution) or coincident (infinitely many solutions). We need to check c₁/c₂: if c₁/c₂ = 5/3, the lines are coincident (infinitely many solutions); if c₁/c₂ ≠ 5/3, the lines are parallel (no solution). A wrong answer (e.g., "unique solution") shows the student does not recognise that equal ratios of a and b mean the lines are NOT intersecting.

questions.q: The system 2x + y = 5 and 4x + 2y = 10 has a₁/a₂ = 2/4 = 1/2, b₁/b₂ = 1/2, c₁/c₂ = 5/10 = 1/2. What type of system is this?
questions.a: Since a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂ = 1/2, the lines are coincident (the same line), so the system has infinitely many solutions (dependent system). A wrong answer (e.g., "unique solution" or "no solution") shows the student does not distinguish between the three cases using all three ratios.

questions.q: Why do two lines with different slopes always intersect at exactly one point?
questions.a: Two lines with different slopes are not parallel. In a plane, two non-parallel lines must cross at exactly one point (Euclid's axiom). If they had the same slope, they would be parallel (no intersection) or coincident (same line, infinitely many intersections). A wrong answer (e.g., "they might not intersect if they are far apart") shows a geometric misconception — in a plane, non-parallel lines always intersect.

questions.q: Given the system x + 2y = 4 and 2x + 3y = 7, find the unique solution using substitution and verify it satisfies both equations.
questions.a: From the first equation: x = 4 − 2y. Substitute into the second: 2(4 − 2y) + 3y = 7 ⇒ 8 − 4y + 3y = 7 ⇒ 8 − y = 7 ⇒ y = 1. Then x = 4 − 2(1) = 2. Solution: (2, 1). Verify: 2 + 2(1) = 4 ✓ and 2(2) + 3(1) = 7 ✓. A wrong answer (e.g., x = 1, y = 2) shows an algebraic error in substitution or solving.
